attributes.residual: REFUTES the dispatch premise that the 77 same-opcode IMMEDIATE rows are ONE systematic displacement family: the census splits them into THREE unrelated families. (F1) 28 rows = the four switch-arm conversion-temp blocks at 0x68-0xc0 / 0x158-0x1a8 / 0x238-0x290 / 0x328-0x378, a role-assignment permutation inside the fixed slot set {760,768,776,784}; STILL OPEN. (F2) 4 rows = the 0x75c-0x770 field-read order; closable by term order but at +2 real (probe 3). (F3) 45 rows = the 8-byte copy store order, CLOSED by this keep. The remaining 51 rows are F1 (28) + F2 (4) + the c7c-cb0 addi scheduling trio (3) + 16 pairing-unreliable edge rows. On F1, the target and ours agree on ONE of the four temps in every arm and rotate the other three: case 3 target {buildW 776, buildH 784, convW 768, convH 760} against ours {768, 784, 760, 776}; case 4 target {buildW 768, buildH 760, convW 776, convH 784} against ours {776, 760, 784, 768}. Reading the four temps in ascending-address order, the target is (buildH, buildW, convW, convH) and ours is (buildH, convH, buildW, convW): the target groups by ROLE across the two expressions, ours groups by EXPRESSION. Four probes across two lanes have now failed to move it (two named-f32-intermediate forms in attempt.pbframemode-view-struct-alignment-and-residual-decomposition.20260901.v1, plus probes 1 and 2 here), so the AXIS OF SOURCE STATEMENT SHAPE IS DEAD for F1 and the next lane needs a different handle on temp creation order.

If `@0x68 stw r4,780(r1)` still reads `stw r4,772(r1)` on our side — i.e. the build temp for the width expression is still 768 and not 776 — the single-web form does not move the temp map either and F1 is closed to every source-level handle, which reclassifies it as pure allocator variance.

If it moves the count it has hit the aRWork promotion cascade and is the compensating pair in a new costume, not an F1 result.
hypothesis.screened_against_target: no — the target's temp addresses at 0x68/0x78/0x8c/0xa8/0xb0/0xb8/0xc0 and their case-4 mirrors are read directly from `fnasm --diff` and are accurate, but the single-web form has never been compiled, and it is NOT screened whether collapsing convH into convW changes the two `g->screen` field stores (the target reloads `lwz r3,16(r30)` between them, which our current form already reproduces).
hypothesis.statement: F1 (the conversion-temp role permutation) is not reachable from the shape of the two conversion STATEMENTS — four probes now say so — but it may be reachable from what else is live across them. In the target, the four temps read in ascending address order are (buildH, buildW, convW, convH): the two BUILD temps are allocated before either CONV temp, which is the allocation a compiler produces when both int-to-double builds are complete before the first double-to-int conversion starts. Ours interleaves them per expression. The untried handle is therefore not the statement shape but whether the two conversions share a single destination web: probe assigning BOTH results through one variable (`convW = (s32)(f32)lbl_80343F04; g->screen->width = convW; convW = (s32)(f32)(lbl_80343F0C / 2); g->screen->height = convW;`), which removes convH entirely and forces the allocator to sequence the two conversions rather than overlap them.
